course.title: Khaemenes Academy Sixth Grade — Middle School Subject-Based 36 Week A++ Curriculum
course.subtitle: Advanced Middle School Foundation · In-House Curriculum · Subject Halls
course.dependencyPolicy: No outside fonts, scripts, images, libraries, or curriculum calls. All pages use local files only.
course.localReviewNote: Designed to exceed a single-state checklist by spanning broad Grade 6 academic, arts, health, world language, technology, inquiry, research, capstone, portfolio, and Grade 7 readiness requirements. Local compliance review is still recommended.

subjects.title: Language Arts & Literacy
subjects.description: Middle school reading, citation, literary analysis, informational text, argument, research, grammar, academic vocabulary, discussion, media literacy, and publication.

subjects.title: Mathematics
subjects.description: Ratios, rates, percent, fraction division, decimals, rational numbers, expressions, equations, inequalities, coordinate planes, area, surface area, volume, statistics, and mathematical modeling.

subjects.title: Science & Engineering
subjects.description: Middle school physical, life, Earth, and space science foundations: matter, energy, forces, ecosystems, Earth systems, weather/climate, engineering design, models, data, and CER reasoning.

subjects.title: Social Studies & Civics
subjects.description: Ancient civilizations, geography, world history foundations, civics, economics, cultures, religions, trade, migration, evidence, primary sources, and informed action.

subjects.title: World Languages & Global Culture
subjects.description: Language learning foundations, cognates, greetings, scripts, cultural comparison, geography of languages, respectful communication, translation awareness, and global citizenship.

subjects.title: Arts, Music & Media
subjects.description: Visual design, music literacy, rhythm, melody, dramatic interpretation, media arts, critique, performance, cultural arts, artist statements, and portfolio curation.

subjects.title: Health, PE & SEL
subjects.description: Physical literacy, fitness planning, nutrition, safety, adolescence health foundations, emotional regulation, executive function, collaboration, leadership, resilience, and self-advocacy.

subjects.title: Technology, Design & Tools
subjects.description: Digital citizenship, keyboarding fluency, file systems, spreadsheets, source notes, charts, accessibility, algorithms, debugging, design thinking, presentations, and ethical media.

subjects.title: Integrated Research Projects
subjects.description: Middle school studios where students research, calculate, model, prototype, write, revise, cite, defend evidence, present publicly, reflect, and build a portfolio.

weeks.title: Middle School Scholar Launch
weeks.theme: Transition systems, binders/files, advisory routines, diagnostic reading/math/science writing, research notebooks, executive function, and portfolio setup
weeks.essentialQuestion: How do middle school scholars organize independence, evidence, and responsibility?

weeks.title: Evidence, Annotation, and Ratios
weeks.theme: Text annotation, quoting/citing evidence, ratios as comparisons, unit language, learning contracts, and notebook systems
weeks.essentialQuestion: How do evidence and comparison help us understand complex ideas?

weeks.title: Rates, Unit Rates, and Informational Text
weeks.theme: Unit rates, tables, graphs, informational text structure, technical vocabulary, and source notes
weeks.essentialQuestion: How can rates and text structures explain change?

weeks.title: Percent, Proportion, and Civic Decisions
weeks.theme: Percent, benchmark fractions/decimals, claims and evidence, surveys, civic choices, and data displays
weeks.essentialQuestion: How can percentages help a community make informed decisions?

weeks.title: Fraction Division and Procedural Writing
weeks.theme: Fraction division, visual models, reciprocal reasoning foundations, procedural writing, critique, and clarity
weeks.essentialQuestion: How can models explain division when the numbers are fractions?

weeks.title: Rational Numbers and Ancient Number Systems
weeks.theme: Integers, rational numbers, number lines, absolute value foundations, ancient number systems, and mathematical history
weeks.essentialQuestion: How have cultures represented numbers and meaning across time?

weeks.title: Coordinate Planes and Geography
weeks.theme: Four-quadrant coordinate planes, maps, scale, geography, ordered pairs, and spatial reasoning
weeks.essentialQuestion: How can coordinates help us describe place, movement, and patterns?

weeks.title: Expressions and Algebraic Thinking
weeks.theme: Variables, expressions, substitution, order of operations, literary symbolism, and precise academic language
weeks.essentialQuestion: How can symbols represent ideas in math, language, and culture?

weeks.title: Equations and Balanced Arguments
weeks.theme: One-step equations, balance models, argument writing, claim/reason/evidence, and academic discussion
weeks.essentialQuestion: How do balance and evidence make arguments stronger?

weeks.title: Inequalities and Decision Rules
weeks.theme: Inequalities, constraints, solution sets, policy rules, design limits, and responsible choices
weeks.essentialQuestion: How do constraints shape solutions and decisions?

weeks.title: Statistics: Questions, Data, and Distribution
weeks.theme: Statistical questions, data collection, dot plots, histograms foundations, center/spread, and data ethics
weeks.essentialQuestion: How can data answer questions while still requiring judgment?

weeks.title: Geometry: Area, Surface Area, and Design
weeks.theme: Area formulas, polygons, nets, surface area, design constraints, and visual communication
weeks.essentialQuestion: How do measurements help designers plan efficient spaces?

weeks.title: Volume and Three-Dimensional Modeling
weeks.theme: Volume of rectangular prisms, fractional edge lengths, models, engineering notebooks, and spatial reasoning
weeks.essentialQuestion: How can 3D models solve real problems?

weeks.title: Matter: Particles, Properties, and Models
weeks.theme: Properties of matter, particle models, density foundations, evidence tables, and scientific explanation
weeks.essentialQuestion: How can invisible particle models explain visible properties?

weeks.title: Thermal Energy and Phase Change
weeks.theme: Thermal energy, temperature, phase changes, graphing, data interpretation, and CER writing
weeks.essentialQuestion: How does energy explain changes in matter?

weeks.title: Forces, Motion, and Systems
weeks.theme: Forces, motion, variables, graphs, system models, fair tests, and technical writing
weeks.essentialQuestion: How do forces and systems explain motion?

weeks.title: Midyear Portfolio and Assessment
weeks.theme: Cumulative review, midterm, research checkpoint, math defense, science notebook audit, and advisory reflection
weeks.essentialQuestion: How can I prove growth across every subject?

weeks.title: Waves, Sound, and Communication
weeks.theme: Wave models, sound, communication, media literacy, rhythm, and information transfer
weeks.essentialQuestion: How do waves carry energy and information?

weeks.title: Light, Vision, and Media Interpretation
weeks.theme: Light, reflection, vision, visual media, diagrams, perspective, and evidence from models
weeks.essentialQuestion: How does light shape what we see and how we interpret media?

weeks.title: Cells, Systems, and Scientific Models
weeks.theme: Cells as systems, structure/function, microscopes as tools, analogies, and explanatory models
weeks.essentialQuestion: How do small structures support living systems?

weeks.title: Ecosystems and Energy Flow
weeks.theme: Food webs, ecosystems, matter/energy flow, human impact, statistics, and environmental stewardship
weeks.essentialQuestion: How do energy and matter move through ecosystems?

weeks.title: Earth Systems and Water
weeks.theme: Geosphere, hydrosphere, atmosphere, biosphere, water cycle, maps, resource use, and stewardship
weeks.essentialQuestion: How do Earth systems interact and affect human life?

weeks.title: Weather, Climate, and Human Patterns
weeks.theme: Weather/climate data, graphs, regional patterns, natural hazards, and community resilience
weeks.essentialQuestion: How can patterns help communities prepare for change?

weeks.title: Ancient River Civilizations
weeks.theme: Mesopotamia, Egypt, Indus, China foundations, rivers, agriculture, writing, trade, and social structures
weeks.essentialQuestion: How did rivers support early civilizations and complex societies?

weeks.title: Belief Systems, Law, and Culture
weeks.theme: Ancient laws, belief systems, cultural practices, art, texts, fairness, and historical empathy
weeks.essentialQuestion: How do beliefs and laws shape community life?

weeks.title: Classical Civilizations and Civic Ideas
weeks.theme: Greece, Rome, civic participation, republics, philosophy, architecture, argument, and historical comparison
weeks.essentialQuestion: How did classical societies influence civic ideas and public life?

weeks.title: Trade Routes, Migration, and Exchange
weeks.theme: Silk Roads foundations, trade, migration, cultural diffusion, economics, maps, and perspective
weeks.essentialQuestion: How do movement and exchange transform societies?

weeks.title: World Languages and Cultural Communication
weeks.theme: Language families, scripts, greetings, cognates, translation limits, cultural respect, and global communication
weeks.essentialQuestion: How does language carry culture and connection?

weeks.title: Research Writing: From Question to Thesis
weeks.theme: Research questions, source evaluation, note-taking, paraphrase, thesis, evidence paragraphs, and citation routines
weeks.essentialQuestion: How do researchers build trustworthy explanations?

weeks.title: Argument, Debate, and Public Speaking
weeks.theme: Claims, reasons, evidence, counterclaims, rebuttal, speaking skills, audience, and respectful debate
weeks.essentialQuestion: How can disagreement become disciplined learning?

weeks.title: Arts, Media, and Message Design
weeks.theme: Visual rhetoric, music/media messages, dramatic interpretation, design choices, and artist statements
weeks.essentialQuestion: How do artists and media makers shape meaning?

weeks.title: Health, Identity, and Responsible Choices
weeks.theme: Nutrition, fitness planning, sleep, stress, digital wellness, adolescent health foundations, and self-advocacy
weeks.essentialQuestion: How do healthy routines support learning and identity?

weeks.title: Technology, Data, and Ethical Creation
weeks.theme: Spreadsheets, charts, algorithms, debugging, file systems, accessibility, source notes, and ethical media
weeks.essentialQuestion: How can tools strengthen evidence without replacing judgment?

weeks.title: A++ Big Question Capstone Research
weeks.theme: Independent inquiry, research plan, source notes, data/math component, science/social model, prototype, and timeline
weeks.essentialQuestion: What serious question can I investigate with evidence, calculation, and design?

weeks.title: Capstone Studio and Oral Defense
weeks.theme: Draft, revise, build, calculate, design, peer critique, presentation media, oral defense, and reflection
weeks.essentialQuestion: How can I make my evidence clear enough to defend publicly?

weeks.title: Final Review and Grade 7 Readiness
weeks.theme: Cumulative final, portfolio defense, certificate, grade 7 readiness, study habits, reflection, and celebration
weeks.essentialQuestion: How am I ready for seventh grade?

requires: Weekly assessment average at or above 80%
Portfolio evidence approved by adult mentor
